steps.title: Prepare sample homogenizing buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 10 mL cell lysis buffer (Invitrogen FNN0021) with 34 µL protease inhibitor (Sigma P7626‑56) and 50 µL phosphatase inhibitor (Sigma P2714‑1).

steps.title: Prepare 0.2 M acetate assay buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve either 16.4 g anhydrous sodium acetate or 27.2 g sodium acetate trihydrate in 800 mL dH₂O, adjust pH to 4.5 with acetic acid, then bring the volume to 1 L with dH₂O.

steps.title: Make β‑secretase substrate stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg β‑secretase substrate (250 µM, Sigma 565758) in 2 mL DMSO, aliquot 100 µL portions, store at –20 °C in opaque tubes (light‑sensitive).

steps.title: Make β‑secretase inhibitor stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg β‑secretase inhibitor (250 µM, Sigma S4562) in 2.42 mL DMSO, aliquot 100 µL portions, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Collect and snap‑freeze tissue
steps.instruction: After dissecting the desired brain region, snap‑freeze samples in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Homogenize brain tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize tissue at a 1 mg : 20 µL ratio with the homogenizing buffer (e.g., 5 mg tissue in 100 µL buffer) using either a FastPrep homogenizer (speed 6.5, 45 s) or a glass‑cone hand homogenizer.

steps.title: Sonicate homogenates
steps.instruction: Sonicate each homogenate 3 × 15 s with cooling intervals to ensure homogeneity before protein quantification.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 RCF for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the supernatant from each tube to a new Eppendorf tube without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Quantify protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of each supernatant using a BCA or Bradford assay and record the value in µg/µL.

steps.title: Optional cell lysate preparation
steps.instruction: For SH‑SY5Y cells, collect cells with the same lysis buffer; adjust buffer volume to achieve desired protein concentration (e.g., lyse cells in a 6‑well plate with 200 µL lysis buffer per well).

steps.title: Transfer raw data to spreadsheet
steps.instruction: Export all fluorescence readings to a spreadsheet program such as Excel or Google Sheets.

steps.title: Perform assay quality control
steps.instruction: Verify that positive control wells give the highest values and negative/background wells give comparable baseline values; proceed only if these criteria are met.

steps.title: Process assay data
steps.instruction: Calculate the mean of technical replicates, normalize as required, group by experimental condition, and report values in relative fluorescent units (RFU).

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Select appropriate statistical tests (e.g., Student’s t‑test, ANOVA for parametric data; Mann‑Whitney U, Kruskal‑Wallis for non‑parametric), set significance threshold (p < 0.05), and perform analysis using software such as GraphPad Prism or R.
